pages.text: At the Guild Fair, Inspector Quill unrolls a scroll so long it trips two judges. 'Licence granted. And a seat on the Guild council.'
Madame Vexley shares your stall and insists it was her idea. The Hooded Stranger lights every lantern without singeing one tent.
The village cheers. Granny Marigold tells everyone she discovered you. Duchess the goat eats the trophy ribbon.
Your little shop is now the finest in the Guild. Somewhere, a cauldron bubbles happily. The end... for now.
Inspector Quill stamps your licence with a small, approving nod. 'Not flashy. Very solid. Clause three would be proud.'
Old faces and new ones drop by for tea now and then. The regulars keep coming back, and the kettle is always on.
You stay the village's cosy corner shop: warm tonics, gossip on tap and a goat who visits daily. The end... for now.
The Guild declines your licence. Quill writes 'chaotic' on a form, crosses it out, and writes 'memorable' instead.
A few things got singed along the way. Vexley is insufferable about it. The dragon sends a very sorry note.
But the village loves you anyway. The bard writes a ballad about your shop: eleven verses, one explosion. The end... for now.
